boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Brown University
boards.description: From student-run grill stations to Thayer Street staples, these late-night spots fuel the Brown community long after the libraries close.

cards.title: Josiah's (Jo's)
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Grill in Vartan Gregorian Quad
cards.notes: Order the signature spicy with cheese at this student-favorite grill, which serves as a social hub for late-night study breaks until 2 AM.
cards.short_summary: A quintessential Brown late-night dining spot known for burgers and fries.
cards.evidence_claim: Josiah's is open everyday from 6 PM to 2 AM at 114 Power Street.
cards.source_title: Josiah's (Jo's) - Brown Dining Services
cards.access_notes: Open until 2:00 AM daily during the academic semester.

cards.title: Baja's Tex Mex Grill
cards.subtitle: Thayer Street Burritos
cards.notes: Visit this Thayer Street staple for late-night burritos and quesadillas; it is a primary destination for students after the campus cafes close.
cards.short_summary: A popular Mexican grill on Thayer Street open until the early morning hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Baja's Tex Mex Grill at 273 Thayer Street is open daily from 10 AM to 2 AM.
cards.source_title: Locations - Baja's
cards.access_notes: Open until 2:00 AM every night.

cards.title: East Side Pockets
cards.subtitle: Middle Eastern Fare on Thayer
cards.notes: Grab a falafel wrap or gyro at this award-winning spot, which has been a Thayer Street fixture for Brown students since 1997.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing Middle Eastern restaurant known for quick service and late hours.
cards.evidence_claim: East Side Pockets is open until late night Monday through Saturday and until 10 PM on Sunday.
cards.source_title: Hours - East Side Pockets
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight or later most nights; check current daily schedule.

cards.title: Antonio's Pizza
cards.subtitle: Creative Slices on Thayer
cards.notes: Try unique toppings like Mac & Cheese or Tortellini on your pizza slice at this bustling late-night corner spot near campus.
cards.short_summary: A Thayer Street pizzeria famous for its wide variety of creative slice combinations.
cards.evidence_claim: Antonio's Pizza at 256 Thayer Street is open daily from 11:00 AM to 1:30 AM.
cards.source_title: Antonio's Pizza by the Slice - Thayer Street District
cards.access_notes: Open until 1:30 AM daily.

cards.title: The Ivy Room
cards.subtitle: Vegetarian-Friendly Late Dining
cards.notes: Head to the lower level of the Sharpe Refectory for smoothies and vegetarian-focused dinner specials during late-night hours.
cards.short_summary: A retail dining location at Brown offering fresh, vegetarian-friendly evening options.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ivy Room is open for dinner Sunday through Thursday from 5:00 PM to 10:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Ivy Room | Dining | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:00 PM on weeknights and Sundays.

cards.title: Andrews Commons
cards.subtitle: North Campus Late-Night Hub
cards.notes: Utilize the pizza station or wok at this North Campus facility, which serves as a major late-night study and dining space for students.
cards.short_summary: A modern dining and study common area located in the Andrews Residence Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Andrews Commons offers dinner and late-night options on weekdays and weekends.
cards.source_title: Andrews Commons | Dining | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Open for dinner and late-night service; check BrownU Mobile app for exact nightly closing.

cards.title: Insomnia Cookies
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Bakery
cards.notes: Order warm cookies for delivery or pickup until the early morning hours at this Thayer Street bakery catering to late-night cravings.
cards.short_summary: A bakery specializing in late-night cookie delivery and walk-in service.
cards.evidence_claim: Insomnia Cookies on Thayer Street typically serves customers until 1 AM or later.
cards.source_title: A guide to Thayer Street's late-night eats
cards.access_notes: Open until 1:00 AM or later daily.

cards.title: Mike's Calzones
cards.subtitle: Thayer Street Deli & Grill
cards.notes: Choose from a wide variety of calzones and sandwiches at this Thayer Street spot that remains open well past midnight for the student crowd.
cards.short_summary: A casual eatery on Thayer Street specializing in calzones and late-night comfort food.
cards.evidence_claim: Mike's Calzones is listed as a top late-night option on Thayer Street, often open past midnight.
cards.source_title: A guide to Thayer Street's late-night eats
cards.access_notes: Open late daily; typically until 1:00 AM or 2:00 AM.

cards.title: Zinneken's Waffles
cards.subtitle: Authentic Belgian Waffles
cards.notes: Enjoy authentic pearl sugar waffles with various toppings at this Angell Street cafe, popular for evening dessert runs.
cards.short_summary: A Belgian waffle cafe located near the heart of Brown's campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Zinneken's at 194 Angell Street is open for online ordering and pickup until 9:40 PM.
cards.source_title: Zinneken's – Home
cards.access_notes: Open until 9:40 PM or 10:00 PM most nights.

cards.title: Blue Room Cafe
cards.subtitle: Campus Center Gathering Spot
cards.notes: While primarily a daytime spot, the Blue Room in the Stephen Robert '62 Campus Center is the central meeting point for students between late-afternoon sessions.
cards.short_summary: A central campus cafe known for its sandwiches, pastries, and community atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Room is located in the Stephen Robert '62 Campus Center at 75 Waterman Street.
cards.source_title: Blue Room Cafe | Dining | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Standard hours are 8:00 AM to 3:00 PM; serves as a key transition spot for evening activities.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional study hubs, specialized labs, and quiet corners that Brown University students use for daily academic life beyond the standard tour stops.

cards.title: Friedman Study Center
cards.subtitle: Sciences Library Level A
cards.notes: Access this 24-hour hub on Level A of the SciLi for collaborative work, featuring group study rooms and over 65 computer workstations.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour collaborative study hub located at the base of the Sciences Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Friedman Study Center is a 24-hour space on Level A of the Sciences Library with 8 private group study rooms and 65+ computer workstations.
cards.source_title: Friedman Study Center - Brown University Library
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours for students with Brown ID swipe access.

cards.title: Willis Reading Room
cards.subtitle: John Hay Library
cards.notes: Study in this grand, quiet space within the special collections library, known for its historic atmosphere and rare book surroundings.
cards.short_summary: A historic and quiet reading room located within the John Hay Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Willis Reading Room is a primary study space located in the John Hay Library, which houses rare books and university archives.
cards.source_title: John Hay Library Home Page - Brown University Library
cards.access_notes: Open to current Brown students, faculty, and staff; check library hours for public access times.

cards.title: The Sunlab
cards.subtitle: CIT Building Room 143
cards.notes: Utilize this primary computing facility for CS students, featuring 73 Linux workstations and 24-hour access during peak times.
cards.short_summary: The main undergraduate computer science lab located in the CIT building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sunlab (CIT 143) is the primary computing resource for computer science undergraduates, featuring 73 PCs running Linux.
cards.source_title: Rooms - Brown CS
cards.access_notes: Available days and evenings; 24-hour access often available for CS students.

cards.title: Global Brown Lounge
cards.subtitle: Page-Robinson Hall Room 310
cards.notes: Visit 'The Globe' for a dedicated community space supporting international students and global learning initiatives.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated lounge for Brown's international community in Page-Robinson Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Global Brown Lounge, or 'The Globe', is located in Page-Robinson Hall room 310 and is open to the community from 9am to 5pm.
cards.source_title: Global Brown Lounge
cards.access_notes: Open 9am-5pm for all; after-hours access available for international students via request.

cards.title: Granoff Multimedia Lab
cards.subtitle: Granoff Center for the Creative Arts
cards.notes: Explore this lab for electronics prototyping, sensor interface development, and physical computing projects.
cards.short_summary: A specialized lab for multimedia and physical computing in the Granoff Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Granoff Center features a multimedia lab and physical media lab supporting electronics prototyping and physical computing.
cards.source_title: The Perry and Marty Granoff Center for the Creative Arts | Brown Arts Institute
cards.access_notes: Building hours vary by season; typically open to students during academic terms.

cards.title: Wernig Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Rockefeller Library 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Graduate students can use this dedicated area featuring a kitchen, eating space, and seminar rooms for focused work.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated reading room and lounge for graduate students in the Rockefeller Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wernig Graduate Student Reading Room is on the 2nd floor of the Rockefeller Library and includes a study area, kitchen, and seminar room.
cards.source_title: Wernig Reading Room | Graduate Student Council - Brown University
cards.access_notes: Restricted to graduate students with Brown ID swipe access.

cards.title: SciLi Meditation Room
cards.subtitle: Sciences Library Room 1219
cards.notes: Find a moment of quiet in this dedicated meditation space; check out the room key from the Level A service desk.
cards.short_summary: A quiet meditation space located on the 12th floor of the Sciences Library.
cards.evidence_claim: A meditation room (1219) is located on Level 12 of the Sciences Library; keys are available at the Level A service desk.
cards.source_title: Sciences Library Stack Guide and Services
cards.access_notes: Key checkout required at the Level A service desk.

cards.title: List Art Student Galleries
cards.subtitle: List Art Building
cards.notes: View rotating exhibitions of student work in these galleries, which host senior capstone shows during the spring semester.
cards.short_summary: Exhibition spaces in the List Art Building dedicated to displaying student artwork.
cards.evidence_claim: The List Art Building houses exhibition spaces primarily dedicated to the display of student work, including Senior Capstone Exhibitions.
cards.source_title: Student Exhibitions and Guidelines | Visual Art | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours: 8:30am-5:00pm during the academic year.

cards.title: Campus Center Lounges
cards.subtitle: Stephen Robert '62 Campus Center
cards.notes: Use these common rooms for impromptu meetings or study sessions in the heart of campus life at Faunce House.
cards.short_summary: Common lounge and meeting spaces available for student use in the Campus Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stephen Robert '62 Campus Center (Faunce House) offers common spaces for impromptu meetings and study use.
cards.source_title: Stephen Robert '62 Campus Center - Student Activities | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Open to all university community members during building hours.

cards.title: Nightingale-Brown House Grounds
cards.subtitle: 357 Benefit Street
cards.notes: Walk through the historic gardens designed by Frederick Law Olmsted at this landmark home, now used for public humanities.
cards.short_summary: Historic grounds and gardens of the Nightingale-Brown House.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nightingale-Brown House grounds include a garden designed by Frederick Law Olmsted in 1890.
cards.source_title: Nightingale-Brown House History | John Nicholas Brown Center
cards.access_notes: Grounds are generally accessible; building use is for faculty, students, and staff of the Center.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover the best social and cultural activities at Brown University that require no admission or purchase, from historic observatory viewings to student-led art tours.

cards.title: Public Viewing Nights
cards.subtitle: Stargazing at the historic 1891 observatory
cards.notes: Visit on Tuesday nights for free telescope viewings of planets and stars. Check the official site for weather updates and seasonal hours before heading up the hill.
cards.short_summary: Free weekly public stargazing sessions using a historic 12-inch refractor telescope.
cards.evidence_claim: Ladd Observatory holds scheduled Public Nights on Tuesday evenings with no admission fee, though free tickets may be required.
cards.source_title: Ladd Observatory | Department of Physics | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Open to the public on Tuesday evenings; check the website for specific start times which vary by season.

cards.title: Contemporary Art Exhibits
cards.subtitle: Modern works in the Philip Johnson-designed List Art Building
cards.notes: Explore rotating exhibitions of contemporary art and works from the permanent collection. The gallery is located on the first floor and is always free to enter.
cards.short_summary: A contemporary art space hosting major exhibitions and public events throughout the year.
cards.evidence_claim: The David Winton Bell Gallery is free and open to the public, featuring contemporary art exhibitions and a collection of over 7,000 works.
cards.source_title: The Bell | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Open daily 11 AM–5 PM during exhibitions; extended hours until 8 PM on Thursdays and Fridays.

cards.title: Special Collection Exhibits
cards.subtitle: Rare books and archives in the Willis Reading Room
cards.notes: Sign in at the front desk to view curated displays of rare manuscripts and artifacts. The historic reading room offers a quiet, grand atmosphere for study.
cards.short_summary: Publicly accessible exhibitions featuring rare items from Brown's special collections and archives.
cards.evidence_claim: Visitors without Brown IDs may visit the John Hay Library to view exhibits and special collections materials during public access hours.
cards.source_title: John Hay Library Home Page - Brown University Library
cards.access_notes: Public access hours are typically weekdays 10 AM–5 PM; visitors must sign in at the entrance.

cards.title: Student-Led Art Tours
cards.subtitle: Guided walks through campus sculptures
cards.notes: Join a 40-minute weekend tour to learn the history behind campus landmarks like the Bronze Bruno. Tours meet at the bear statue on the College Green.
cards.short_summary: Free, student-curated walking tours exploring Brown's extensive outdoor public art collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Brown Arts Institute offers free, student-led public art tours every Saturday and Sunday from April through November.
cards.source_title: Public Art Tours | Brown Arts Institute
cards.access_notes: Tours run Saturdays and Sundays at 1 PM; no advance registration is required for these outdoor walks.

cards.title: A Cappella Arch Sings
cards.subtitle: Live vocal performances under the archway
cards.notes: Catch one of Brown's many a cappella groups performing in this acoustic hotspot. These informal concerts are frequent on weekend evenings and always free.
cards.short_summary: Informal, free vocal performances by student a cappella groups utilizing the arch's natural acoustics.
cards.evidence_claim: Student a cappella groups like The Higher Keys and Brown Derbies frequently perform free 'arch sings' under Wayland Arch.
cards.source_title: The Brown Derbies: Home
cards.access_notes: Performances are typically unscheduled or announced via student social media; most common on Friday and Saturday nights.

cards.title: Granoff Center Exhibitions
cards.subtitle: Interdisciplinary art in the Granoff Center
cards.notes: Visit the first-floor gallery for multimedia installations and student-curated shows. The building itself is a modern architectural landmark on Angell Street.
cards.short_summary: A gallery space within the Granoff Center showcasing thematic and research-based art exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cohen Gallery in the Granoff Center is free and open to the public, featuring rotating thematic exhibitions.
cards.source_title: Cohen Gallery | Brown Arts Institute
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Friday 9 AM–10 PM, with weekend hours from 12 PM to 6 PM or 8 PM.

cards.title: Main Green Socializing
cards.subtitle: The central hub of campus life
cards.notes: Join students for frisbee, spikeball, or picnicking on the grass. It is the primary spot for people-watching and outdoor relaxation between classes.
cards.short_summary: The iconic central lawn of Brown University used for recreation, study, and major student events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Main Green is a public campus space where students and visitors can lounge, picnic, and play lawn games for free.
cards.source_title: 10 things to do while you're on College Hill - The Brown Daily Herald
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for public use; subject to university green space policies for organized events.

cards.title: Entrepreneurship Workshops
cards.subtitle: Free talks and pitch events
cards.notes: Attend open workshops and guest speaker sessions to learn about startups. Most events are free and provide a great way to network with the local community.
cards.short_summary: A hub for student innovation offering free workshops, talks, and networking events open to the community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nelson Center hosts various free events, including the B-Lab Expo and guest speaker talks, which are often open to the public.
cards.source_title: Events - Nelson Center for Entrepreneurship - Brown University
cards.access_notes: Events are held throughout the academic year; check the online calendar for specific public-facing sessions.

cards.title: Free Group Fitness
cards.subtitle: Student-only workout sessions
cards.notes: Brown students can join yoga, pilates, and spin classes at no extra cost. Bring your student ID to the Nelson Fitness Center to participate.
cards.short_summary: Complimentary group fitness classes offered to all active Brown University students.
cards.evidence_claim: Brown students receive free access to group fitness classes at the Nelson Fitness Center as part of their student benefits.
cards.source_title: I Tried Five of Brown U's Free Workout Classes
cards.access_notes: Restricted to Brown and RISD ID holders; classes require registration via the BFit app.

cards.title: Student Art Galleries
cards.subtitle: Exhibitions by Visual Art concentrators
cards.notes: Walk through the upper floors of the List Art Building to see student capstone projects and juried shows. These galleries highlight emerging campus talent.
cards.short_summary: Exhibition spaces dedicated to showcasing the work of Brown University visual art students.
cards.evidence_claim: The List Art Building houses exhibition spaces primarily dedicated to the display of student work, which are free to visit.
cards.source_title: Our Spaces - Visual Art | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Open 8:30 AM–5:00 PM during the academic year; visitors should check in at the main office if visiting upper floors.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Choose ten distinct study environments. Verify access rules, room or reservation constraints, and the physical affordance that makes each useful.

cards.title: Willis Reading Room
cards.subtitle: John Hay Library
cards.notes: Study in a grand, historic setting with high ceilings and long wooden tables. Access is available to Brown ID holders via card swipe at the accessible entrance.
cards.short_summary: A historic, quiet study hall within the John Hay Library known for its grand architecture.
cards.evidence_claim: The Willis Reading Room is located at the John Hay Library and is available for quiet study to Brown ID holders.
cards.source_title: John Hay Library Access
cards.access_notes: Open to Brown and RISD ID holders; check library site for seasonal hours and temporary closures.

cards.title: Friedman Study Center
cards.subtitle: Sciences Library
cards.notes: Utilize 27,000 square feet of collaborative and individual space. Level A features over 65 computers and expert technology consultants for student support.
cards.short_summary: A modern, multi-level study hub located at the base of the Sciences Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Friedman Study Center offers more than 27,000 square feet of study and social space on Level A of the Sciences Library.
cards.source_title: Friedman Study Center - Brown University Library
cards.access_notes: Swipe access required for entry; Level A is dedicated to study spaces.

cards.title: Rockefeller Library Carrels
cards.subtitle: Rockefeller Library
cards.notes: Reserve a designated quiet desk with shelves and power outlets. Carrels are located on the perimeter of the stacks on every level except the main floor.
cards.short_summary: Individual study desks located within the library stacks for focused, quiet work.
cards.evidence_claim: Carrels are study spaces for quiet, individual study located on the perimeter of the stacks at the Rockefeller Library.
cards.source_title: Reserve Rooms, Lockers and Carrels - Brown University Library
cards.access_notes: Active Brown students and faculty can reserve carrels; materials can be checked out to the carrel.

cards.title: Campus Center Common Spaces
cards.subtitle: Faunce House
cards.notes: Find a spot in the common rooms or lounges for impromptu study sessions. This central hub is open daily during the academic year starting at 7:00am.
cards.short_summary: A central social and study hub with various lounges and common areas for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stephen Robert '62 Campus Center has rooms and common spaces available for impromptu meetings and study use.
cards.source_title: Common Spaces | Student Activities | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Open to the campus community; hours are typically 7:00am to midnight during the academic year.

cards.title: Sidney E. Frank Digital Studio
cards.subtitle: Rockefeller Library
cards.notes: Access specialized equipment for digital scholarship and multimedia projects. This space supports the development and presentation of digital research.
cards.short_summary: A technology-focused study space in the Rockefeller Library for digital project work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sidney E. Frank Digital Studio provides physical spaces for the development and support of digital scholarship.
cards.source_title: Programs and Spaces - Brown University Library
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of the Rockefeller Library; available during library hours.

cards.title: The Sunlab
cards.subtitle: CIT Building
cards.notes: Work in the primary computing facility for computer science students. It features over 70 Linux workstations and is often available late into the evening.
cards.short_summary: A high-capacity computer lab in the CIT building primarily for CS coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sunlab, located in CIT 143, is the primary computing resource for computer science undergraduates.
cards.source_title: Rooms - Brown CS
cards.access_notes: Primarily for students with CS course accounts; located in Room 143 of the CIT.

cards.title: MacMillan Reading Room
cards.subtitle: John Carter Brown Library
cards.notes: Study in a quiet, specialized environment by making a research appointment. This room is dedicated to consulting the library's rare book collections.
cards.short_summary: A specialized reading room for researchers at the John Carter Brown Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The John Carter Brown Library welcomes researchers to consult collections in the W. Duncan MacMillan Reading Room by appointment.
cards.source_title: Reading Room Appointments - John Carter Brown Library
cards.access_notes: Appointments are required for all research visits; open Monday-Friday with limited hours.

cards.title: Multimedia Lab
cards.subtitle: Granoff Center
cards.notes: Use this creative space for multidisciplinary work and digital production. The center is designed to catalyze collaboration across arts and sciences.
cards.short_summary: A creative lab space in the Granoff Center for arts and technology projects.
cards.evidence_claim: The Granoff Center features a multimedia lab and flexible production spaces for multidisciplinary work.
cards.source_title: The Perry and Marty Granoff Center for the Creative Arts
cards.access_notes: Open to Brown ID holders; check building hours for seasonal changes.

cards.title: Orwig Music Library
cards.subtitle: Young Orchard Avenue
cards.notes: Find a quiet spot among the music collections and scores. This library provides a specialized environment for music-related study and research.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, specialized library focused on music scores and recordings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Orwig Music Library holds materials supporting music study and research and is restricted to Brown and RISD ID holders.
cards.source_title: Orwig Music Library - Brown University Library
cards.access_notes: Swipe access required; check website for current operating hours.

cards.title: Racial Justice Resource Center
cards.subtitle: Rockefeller Library
cards.notes: Gather for research and learning in this dedicated space on the second floor. It is designed for the Brown community to advance ideas of racial justice.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated space in the Rockefeller Library for research and gathering around racial justice.
cards.evidence_claim: The Racial Justice Resource Center is located on the second floor of the Rockefeller Library for research and gathering.
cards.source_title: Programs and Spaces - Brown University Library
cards.access_notes: Available to members of the Brown community during library hours.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the commercial corridors and historic streets that define student life in Providence's East Side and Jewelry District.

cards.title: The Student Commercial Hub
cards.subtitle: Thayer Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this primary commercial strip to visit the Brown Bookstore or grab a quick meal at local favorites like East Side Pockets.
cards.short_summary: Thayer Street is the central commercial artery for Brown students, featuring a dense mix of independent shops and global eateries.
cards.evidence_claim: Thayer Street is described as the heart of the Brown University neighborhood, catering to the college crowd with dozens of unique businesses.
cards.source_title: Brown ❤️ Providence campaign launching Feb. 14 | Office of the President
cards.access_notes: Public street with high pedestrian activity; most businesses open late to accommodate student schedules.

cards.title: Fox Point's Eclectic Strip
cards.subtitle: Wickenden Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore this historic street in Fox Point for independent art galleries, coffee houses, and unique vintage finds.
cards.short_summary: Wickenden Street offers a bohemian atmosphere with a mix of Portuguese heritage and modern student-friendly cafes.
cards.evidence_claim: Wickenden Street is a popular destination for students, featuring numerous independent shops, art galleries, and restaurants.
cards.source_title: Living in Providence | Watson School of International and Public Affairs - Brown University
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare located south of the main campus in the Fox Point neighborhood.

cards.title: The Creative Arts Corridor
cards.subtitle: Angell Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the Granoff Center for the Creative Arts or the Lindemann Performing Arts Center along this major campus-adjacent street.
cards.short_summary: Angell Street serves as a major east-west thoroughfare housing several of Brown's premier arts and research facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lindemann Performing Arts Center and Granoff Center are located along Angell Street, featuring public outdoor communal spaces.
cards.source_title: Outdoor/Communal Space | Brown Arts Institute
cards.access_notes: Public street; outdoor seating at the Lindemann Tribune is available for public use.

cards.title: The Campus Gateway
cards.subtitle: Waterman Street Corridor
cards.notes: Access the Stephen Robert '62 Campus Center and the Watson Center for Information Technology on this central street.
cards.short_summary: Waterman Street is a primary campus artery connecting the Main Green to the eastern residential and academic quads.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stephen Robert '62 Campus Center is located at 75 Waterman Street, serving as a hub for student activities.
cards.source_title: Contact Us - Student Activities | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Public street; the Campus Center is open to students and visitors during academic hours.

cards.title: The Riverfront Connection
cards.subtitle: South Main Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk along the Providence River to reach the Jewelry District and the Warren Alpert Medical School facilities.
cards.short_summary: South Main Street connects the historic College Hill area to the modern research hubs in the Jewelry District.
cards.evidence_claim: Brown has invested significantly in the Jewelry District, with facilities like the Medical School located near South Main Street.
cards.source_title: Brown purchases its portion of South Street Landing in Providence's Jewelry District
cards.access_notes: Public street with pedestrian walkways along the riverfront.

cards.title: Upscale East Side Dining
cards.subtitle: Wayland Square Corridor
cards.notes: Visit this neighborhood square for a quieter study spot at local bakeries or to browse independent bookstores.
cards.short_summary: Wayland Square is a sophisticated shopping and dining district located a short walk east of the main campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Wayland Square is identified as a walkable neighborhood near Brown with international food markets and boutiques.
cards.source_title: Providence and Rhode Island - Global Brown Center
cards.access_notes: Public commercial district; easily accessible via the RIPTA bus or a 15-minute walk from campus.

cards.title: The Local Neighborhood Strip
cards.subtitle: Hope Street Corridor
cards.notes: Head north to find local specialty markets and community-focused businesses supported by the Brown community.
cards.short_summary: Hope Street offers a residential-commercial mix with local grocery stores and small businesses popular with graduate students.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope Street is highlighted as a key area for local spending and community support through the 'Brown Loves Providence' initiative.
cards.source_title: Through 'Brown Loves Providence,' Brown community members turn appreciation into action
cards.access_notes: Public street; northern sections feature a high concentration of local shops and eateries.

cards.title: The Residential Spine
cards.subtitle: Brook Street Corridor
cards.notes: See the new student housing developments and access the Nelson Fitness Center along this north-south street.
cards.short_summary: Brook Street serves as a primary residential corridor, housing many of Brown's newest dormitory projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Brown has constructed new on-campus housing on both sides of Brook Street between Charlesfield and Power Streets.
cards.source_title: Brook Street Residence Halls - Facilities and Campus Operations
cards.access_notes: Public street; residential buildings require card access for entry.

cards.title: The Mile of History
cards.subtitle: Benefit Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this historic street to see one of the highest concentrations of Colonial architecture in the United States.
cards.short_summary: Benefit Street is a world-renowned historic district featuring beautifully preserved 18th and 19th-century homes.
cards.evidence_claim: Benefit Street is a designated historic district known for its architectural significance and proximity to the RISD Museum.
cards.source_title: Campus Map | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Public street; ideal for architectural walking tours.

cards.title: The Innovation Corridor
cards.subtitle: Eddy Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit South Street Landing or the Rhode Island Nursing Education Center in this rapidly developing district.
cards.short_summary: Eddy Street is the backbone of the Jewelry District, housing administrative offices and professional schools.
cards.evidence_claim: South Street Landing, located at 350 Eddy Street, is a $220 million redevelopment project housing Brown administrative offices.
cards.source_title: South Street Landing | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Public street; South Street Landing lobby is accessible to visitors with proper identification.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From fictitious professors to midnight organ recitals, Brown University's traditions reflect its unique blend of intellectual rigor and creative spirit.

cards.title: The Van Wickle Gates Procession
cards.subtitle: Opening Convocation and Commencement
cards.notes: Walk through the center gates only twice: once inward as a freshman and once outward as a graduate. Passing through more often is said to curse your graduation or marriage prospects.
cards.short_summary: A ceremonial passage through the university's main gates marking the beginning and end of a student's journey.
cards.evidence_claim: The center gates remain closed except for Opening Convocation (opened inward) and Commencement (opened outward).
cards.source_title: Van Wickle Gates - Brown 250
cards.access_notes: The center gates are physically locked except during specific university ceremonies.

cards.title: Carberry Day
cards.subtitle: Every Friday the 13th
cards.notes: Donate loose change to 'cracked pots' for the Carberry Fund on Friday the 13th. It honors Brown's fictional Professor of Psychoceramics, legendary for his 'future late wife' Laura.
cards.short_summary: A recurring celebration of Brown's most famous fictitious professor, occurring every Friday the 13th.
cards.evidence_claim: Every Friday the 13th is Carberry Day, where funds are collected in cracked pots for the Josiah S. Carberry Fund.
cards.source_title: Brown Traditions: Josiah S. Carberry | Alumni & Friends
cards.access_notes: Donation pots are typically placed in university libraries and dining halls on the designated day.

cards.title: Midnight Halloween Organ Recital
cards.subtitle: October 31st at 11:59 PM
cards.notes: Bring a blanket and pillow to Sayles Hall to hear spooky classics on the 1903 Hutchings-Votey pipe organ. Costumes are encouraged for this atmospheric midnight performance.
cards.short_summary: An annual midnight concert featuring haunting music on one of the world's largest remaining pipe organs.
cards.evidence_claim: The annual Halloween Midnight Organ Recital takes place October 31st at 11:59 pm in Sayles Hall.
cards.source_title: 2025 Halloween Midnight Organ Recital | Events | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Entry is limited to the first 450 students with ID; others can watch a livestream on the Main Green.

cards.title: Campus Dance
cards.subtitle: Commencement Weekend
cards.notes: Dance under thousands of paper lanterns on the College Green. This multi-generational ball brings together alumni and graduating seniors to kick off Commencement weekend.
cards.short_summary: A massive outdoor dance party under paper lanterns that serves as the official start of Reunion and Commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Dance transforms the heart of College Hill into an open-air ballroom with glowing paper lanterns.
cards.source_title: Campus Dance | Alumni & Friends | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Tickets are required for entry; the event is held on the Friday evening of Reunion Weekend.

cards.title: The Pembroke Seal Curse
cards.subtitle: Alumnae Hall Steps
cards.notes: Avoid stepping on the bronze seal on the steps of Alumnae Hall. Legend says women who step on it will get pregnant, and men will never graduate.
cards.short_summary: A campus superstition regarding a bronze seal that students carefully avoid to protect their academic and personal futures.
cards.evidence_claim: A decades-old myth warns that stepping on the Pembroke Seal leads to pregnancy for women or failure to graduate for men.
cards.source_title: Walking through the Van Wickle Gates: Commencement and campus curses
cards.access_notes: The seal is located on the steps leading to Alumnae Hall on the Pembroke Campus.

cards.title: The Ratty Sit
cards.subtitle: Sharpe Refectory
cards.notes: Spend an entire day—from opening at 7:30 AM to closing at 7:30 PM—inside the 'Ratty' dining hall. It is a rite of passage for students testing their endurance and appetite.
cards.short_summary: A student-led endurance challenge involving staying in the main dining hall for its entire operating duration.
cards.evidence_claim: The 'Ratty Challenge' involves students spending the entire day at the Sharpe Refectory.
cards.source_title: Which activities top Brown students' bucket lists?
cards.access_notes: Requires a meal swipe or payment for entry; students must remain inside the facility to complete the challenge.

cards.title: Spring Weekend
cards.subtitle: Annual Music Festival
cards.notes: Enjoy a weekend of live music on the Green. Organized by the Brown Concert Agency since 1950, it has hosted legends from Bob Dylan to Kendrick Lamar.
cards.short_summary: Brown's signature annual music festival featuring major national acts and student performers.
cards.evidence_claim: Spring Weekend is a student-organized music festival hosted annually in April at Brown University.
cards.source_title: Spring Weekend - Wikipedia
cards.access_notes: The event is typically free for Brown students but requires a wristband for entry to the fenced concert area.

cards.title: Senior Sing
cards.subtitle: Commencement Finale
cards.notes: Join the graduating class on the steps of Sayles Hall for a final musical tribute. This tradition dates back to the mid-19th century as part of Class Day celebrations.
cards.short_summary: A sentimental musical tradition where graduating seniors gather to sing together one last time.
cards.evidence_claim: Graduating seniors take to the steps of Sayles Hall for the time-honored Brown tradition: Senior Sing.
cards.source_title: Campus Dance | Alumni & Friends | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Occurs late Friday night during Commencement weekend following Campus Dance.

cards.title: The Baccalaureate Procession
cards.subtitle: Multi-faith Service
cards.notes: Follow the Chinese lions and drumming groups to the First Baptist Church. This service blends diverse spiritual traditions with the medieval custom of 'sermonic oration.'
cards.short_summary: A colorful, multi-faith procession and service for graduating seniors held in the historic First Baptist Church.
cards.evidence_claim: The Baccalaureate ceremony includes a procession led by Chinese lions and Japanese drumming groups.
cards.source_title: A distinctly Brown take on an age-old tradition — Class of 2016 celebrates Baccalaureate
cards.access_notes: Seating inside the church is reserved for seniors; guests can watch via livestream from other locations.

cards.title: Gigs on the Grass
cards.subtitle: Fall Student Music Showcase
cards.notes: Catch local student bands and solo acts performing all day on the Main Green. It is a relaxed fall tradition that showcases the diverse musical talent within the student body.
cards.short_summary: A day-long outdoor concert series featuring student performers on the university's central lawn.
cards.evidence_claim: Gigs on the Grass presents student acts throughout the day on the Main Green.
cards.source_title: Gigs on the Grass to take on Main Green Saturday
cards.access_notes: Open to the public and held outdoors on the university's main lawn.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Brown University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Process Through the Gates
cards.subtitle: The Official Start of Your Brown Journey
cards.notes: Walk through the center gates as they open inward for Convocation. This tradition marks your official entry into the Brown community; you only pass through again at graduation.
cards.short_summary: The iconic gates that open only for Convocation and Commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: The center gates remain closed except for two occasions: they are opened inward to welcome first-year students during Opening Convocation and outward at Commencement.
cards.source_title: Van Wickle Gates - Brown 250
cards.access_notes: Open to the public for viewing; center gates only open for specific university ceremonies.

cards.title: Join the Campus Game Night
cards.subtitle: Evening Social on the Historic Lawn
cards.notes: Head to the Main Green on Saturday night for board games and casual conversation. It is a central hub for meeting fellow first-years in a low-pressure outdoor setting.
cards.short_summary: The central lawn of Brown's campus and a primary social gathering spot.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Game Night is held on the Main Green during Orientation weekend, featuring board games and conversations with student representatives.
cards.source_title: Campus Life Events
cards.access_notes: Orientation events typically require an NSO lanyard for entry; the Green itself is public.

cards.title: Grab a Muffin at the Blue Room
cards.subtitle: A Morning Ritual in Faunce House
cards.notes: Visit this campus staple in the Stephen Robert '62 Campus Center. It is famous for its muffins and sandwiches, serving as a popular weekend morning meeting spot.
cards.short_summary: A beloved campus cafe located in the Stephen Robert '62 Campus Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Room is a retail cafe in the Campus Center known for its deli, muffins, and weekend hours from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Blue Room Cafe | Dining | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Open weekends 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM during the academic year.

cards.title: Walk the Thayer Street Corridor
cards.subtitle: The Heart of Student Commerce
cards.notes: Explore the shops and eateries lining this vibrant street. From the Brown Bookstore to local favorites like East Side Pockets, it is the go-to for off-campus essentials.
cards.short_summary: The main commercial street adjacent to Brown's campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Thayer Street is a vibrant area with dozens of unique businesses catering to the college crowd, including dining and shopping.
cards.source_title: Thayer Street Providence | Dining, Shopping, Local Culture
cards.access_notes: Public street; individual business hours vary.

cards.title: Browse the Galleries for Free
cards.subtitle: World-Class Art with Your Brown ID
cards.notes: Use your Brown ID for free admission to this renowned museum. It is a quiet weekend escape featuring everything from ancient Egyptian artifacts to contemporary design.
cards.short_summary: The art museum of the Rhode Island School of Design, accessible to Brown students.
cards.evidence_claim: Brown students receive free admission to the RISD Museum with a valid Brown ID through the Brown Arts Pass program.
cards.source_title: Brown Arts Pass
cards.access_notes: Free for Brown students with ID; open Tuesday-Sunday 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM.

cards.title: Watch the Sunset Over Providence
cards.subtitle: A Scenic View of the City Skyline
cards.notes: Walk a few blocks from campus to see the statue of Roger Williams and enjoy the best view of downtown. It is a classic spot for students to gather at dusk.
cards.short_summary: An elevated park offering panoramic views of the Providence skyline.
cards.evidence_claim: Prospect Terrace is a student paradise for gathering and the perfect vantage point for sunsets over the city.
cards.source_title: View from the Top | Hey Rhody Media Co.
cards.access_notes: Public park; open daily from dawn to dusk.

cards.title: Visit the Fitness Loft
cards.subtitle: Recreation and Wellness on Hope Street
cards.notes: Check out the 10,000-square-foot fitness loft to stay active. It is the primary gym for students and offers a social lobby space with a cafe.
cards.short_summary: Brown's primary indoor athletic and fitness facility.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nelson Fitness Center features a 10,000 square foot fitness loft and is open on weekends from 8:00 AM to 9:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Nelson Fitness Center - Brown University Recreation
cards.access_notes: Brown ID required for entry; weekend hours are 8:00 AM - 9:00 PM.

cards.title: Find Your Study Nook at 'The Rock'
cards.subtitle: The Main Humanities and Social Sciences Library
cards.notes: Explore the stacks and find a quiet place to read. The first floor offers digital studios, while upper floors provide classic library silence and views of the city.
cards.short_summary: The primary research library for humanities and social sciences at Brown.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rockefeller Library, known as 'the Rock,' is the primary teaching and research library for humanities and social sciences.
cards.source_title: John D. Rockefeller Jr. Library
cards.access_notes: Brown ID swipe access required; weekend hours typically start at 10:00 AM or 12:00 PM.

cards.title: Discover the Innovation Hub
cards.subtitle: Workshops and Community for New Ideas
cards.notes: Stop by the Nelson Center to learn about the 'Innovation Dojo' for first-years. It is a collaborative space for students looking to develop new ventures.
cards.short_summary: A hub for interdisciplinary entrepreneurship and student-led ventures.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nelson Center offers the Innovation Dojo, a workshop specifically for first- and second-year students to develop ventures.
cards.source_title: Nelson Center for Entrepreneurship
cards.access_notes: Open to students for workshops and collaborative work; check calendar for specific events.

cards.title: Explore the Activities Fair
cards.subtitle: Connect with 450+ Student Groups
cards.notes: Walk through the rows of tables on the Main Green to find your community. From club sports to a capella, this is the best way to see the breadth of campus life.
cards.short_summary: The annual fair where student organizations recruit new members.
cards.evidence_claim: The annual Fall Student Activities Fair takes place on the Main Green, featuring recognized student organizations.
cards.source_title: Fall 2025 Student Activities Fair | Events | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Typically held on the first Thursday or Friday of the semester; open to all students.
